## Problem

Differentiating induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) into specific cell types requires precise control of culture conditions. Manual optimization is time-consuming and often yields suboptimal results. We needed a systematic approach to identify optimal differentiation parameters.

## Solution

Implemented a data-driven optimization framework:

- Design of experiments (DOE) approach for systematic parameter testing
- High-throughput data collection from flow cytometry and qPCR
- Statistical modeling to identify key variables affecting differentiation efficiency
- Machine learning models to predict optimal culture conditions
- Automated data visualization dashboard for real-time monitoring

The framework enabled rapid optimization of differentiation protocols with minimal experimental iterations.

## Technologies

- **Python**: Data analysis and modeling (scipy, statsmodels)
- **Machine Learning**: Regression models and optimization algorithms
- **R**: Statistical analysis and experimental design
- **Flow Cytometry Data**: Automated processing and quality control

## Outcomes

- Improved differentiation efficiency by 40% compared to baseline protocols
- Reduced optimization time from 6 months to 6 weeks
- Created reusable framework applicable to multiple cell types
- Established data pipeline for continuous process improvement
- Supported manufacturing scale-up with validated protocols

This project showcases how combining scientific domain knowledge with statistical rigor and machine learning can accelerate therapeutic cell production.
